newsitem.title: USA: Molten Metal says funds cut by $12 mln.
newsitem.headline: Molten Metal says funds cut by $12 mln.

text.p: Molten Metal Technology Inc said the U.S. Department of Energy's decision to award the company $12 million less than the environmental technology firm originally expected, plus its decision to delay a Japanese venture, accounted for its whopping stock loss on Monday.
Molten Metal shares tumbled 13-3/8 to 14-3/4, shearing off nearly half the company's market capitalization from roughly $780 million to $408 million.

"The $12 million in revenues we lost, the way it was set up was about $0.38 a share, and delaying the Nichimen, that's virtually everything in the short term," Molten Metal's chief financial officer Benjamin Downs said on a conference call, accounting for the drop in the stock.

He said the company's delayed entry into the fly ash market with a decision to put off for a year a planned joint venture with NKK Plant Engineery Corp, a subsidiary of NKK Corp and Nichimen Corp, was also hurting the stock price.
"That affects construction revenues by moving the planned revenues from 1997 to 1998," Downs said.

William Haney, Molten's chairman, said the delay came because "the negotions are going slower than we expected" but stressed that Nichimen is still "very interested in our technology and we have four or five other companies also interested."

Downs said the burn rate for the first half of 1996 from an operation basis was roughly break in terms of cash. He said he expected the a burn rate of about $2 million a month during the second half of the year, or roughly the revenue shortfall from the cut in government funds.
He said for calendar 1997, he expected a cash positive burn rate. Molten Metal also stressed that its current liquidity was not in any short-term danger from the changes.

Downs said capital expenditures for the second half of 1996 were expected to be roughly $45 million and about the same for all of 1997. To fund the expenditures, he said the company is planning a $40 million tax-exempt bond offering for its Oakridge, Tennessee facility in the first quarter.

It said it would also delay some commercial contracts until the middle of 1997 after it demonstrated its technology at a Hoeschst Celanese plant, which is currently under construction. "Our position to customers is, why don't you just wait until April, why don't you wait and see?," Molten Metal said.
Molten Metal first announced the shortfall and the delay in a conference call to sell-side analysts on Sunday night to guide their estimates lower.
Deutsche Morgan Grenfell and Alex Brown & Sons Inc cut the company's stock rating and profit estimates on Monday.

Rod Lache of Morgan Grenfell slashed the company's third quarter estimates to a loss of $0.03 a share from a prior estimate of $0.23 a share and fourth quarter profits to nil from $0.12 a share. He also cut 1997 earnings per share estimates in half, to $0.60 a share from $1.20 and 1998 profits to $1.50 a share from $2.10 in a research report.
